## RtpMidiBox.kt { #rtpmidibox-kt }

The box-facing side of RTP-MIDI: `rtpMidi(...)` opens or joins an AppleMIDI network session that
a DAW, an iPad app or macOS *MIDI Network Setup* can connect to, and `rtpMidiDiscover()` lists the
sessions already on the network.

Sessions are shared per port across boxes and outlive a stopped box; each box's listeners are
replaced when it re-runs. The wire protocol is in `RtpMidiSession.kt` and `RtpMidiCodec.kt`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/io/midi/rtp/RtpMidiBox.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/io/midi/rtp/RtpMidiBox/)

**Used in:** [Network MIDI: RTP-MIDI sessions](../rtp_midi.md)

## RtpMidiCodec.kt { #rtpmidicodec-kt }

Packet encoding and decoding for RTP-MIDI (RFC 6295) and the AppleMIDI session commands around it.

`RtpMidiLoopbackTest` covers running status, long headers, segmented SysEx, real-time bytes inside
running status, skipped recovery journals and session-packet round trips.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/io/midi/rtp/RtpMidiCodec.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/io/midi/rtp/RtpMidiCodec/)

## RtpMidiSession.kt { #rtpmidisession-kt }

A UDP AppleMIDI session that accepts or sends invitations, keeps peer clocks in sync and sends and
receives MIDI as `javax.sound.midi` messages.

Most box code reaches it through `rtpMidi(...)` in `RtpMidiBox.kt`; `RtpMidiLoopbackTest`
connects two sessions over loopback UDP.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/io/midi/rtp/RtpMidiSession.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/io/midi/rtp/RtpMidiSession/)

## MqttBox.kt { #mqttbox-kt }

The box-facing MQTT surface: `mqtt` and `mqtt(url)` return a [`BoxMqtt`](networking.md#mqttbox-kt-boxmqtt) for publishing and
subscribing, and `mqttBroker(port)` starts an embedded broker.

Callbacks arrive on the main Runloop, so they can touch boxes, sliders and graphics directly.
Connections and brokers outlive a stopped box and are shared by url and port; subscriptions belong
to the box that made them. [`MqttConnections`](networking.md#mqttbox-kt-mqttconnections) holds that shared state.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/io/mqtt/MqttBox.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/io/mqtt/MqttBox/)

**Used in:** [MQTT: sensors, devices and brokers](../mqtt.md)

## MqttBroker.kt { #mqttbroker-kt }

An embedded MQTT 3.1.1 broker, [`MqttBroker`](networking.md#mqttbroker-kt-mqttbroker), for talking MQTT inside Field with nothing else
installed.

It binds to loopback by default; bind `"0.0.0.0"` to accept devices on the local network. The
class documentation lists which parts of the protocol it implements.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/io/mqtt/MqttBroker.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/io/mqtt/MqttBroker/)

## MqttClient.kt { #mqttclient-kt }

An MQTT 3.1.1 client over plain TCP, [`MqttClient`](networking.md#mqttclient-kt-mqttclient), with the message, subscription and connection
event types it hands back.

The client reconnects with backoff, re-subscribes after a reconnect and re-sends unacknowledged
QoS 1 publishes. Box code normally reaches it through `mqtt`, which routes callbacks onto the main
Runloop.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/io/mqtt/MqttClient.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/io/mqtt/MqttClient/)

The future completes when the message has left (QoS 0) or been acknowledged (QoS 1/2). A QoS 0 message published while disconnected is dropped and its future fails; QoS 1 is queued and sent on reconnect. |

## MqttCodec.kt { #mqttcodec-kt }

The MQTT 3.1.1 wire format: the [`MqttPacket`](networking.md#mqttcodec-kt-mqttpacket) types, [`Mqtt.encode`](networking.md#mqttcodec-kt--mqtt--encode) and [`Mqtt.read`](networking.md#mqttcodec-kt--mqtt--read) to convert
them to and from bytes, and [`MqttTopic`](networking.md#mqttcodec-kt-mqtttopic) for topic names and `+` / `#` filter matching.

The client and the embedded broker both use this codec. `MqttCodecTest` and
`MqttTopicSubsumesTest` cover it.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/io/mqtt/MqttCodec.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/io/mqtt/MqttCodec/)

Topic names, topic filters and the `+` / `#` wildcards (MQTT 3.1.1 §4.7).

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="mqttcodec-kt--mqtttopic--isvalidname"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">isValidName</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">topic</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/io/mqtt/MqttCodec/#L299) | A name you can publish to: non-empty, no wildcards. |
| <a id="mqttcodec-kt--mqtttopic--isvalidfilter"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">isValidFilter</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">filter</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/io/mqtt/MqttCodec/#L302) | A filter you can subscribe to: `+` fills a whole level, `#` only as the whole last level. |
| <a id="mqttcodec-kt--mqtttopic--subsumes"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">subsumes</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">f</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">g</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/io/mqtt/MqttCodec/#L318) | Whether every topic `g` matches is also matched by [`f`](workspace.md#stdlib-kt--f) (both valid filters). `a/#` subsumes `a`, `a/+` and `a/b/c`; `a/+` subsumes `a/b`; `#` and `+/#` subsume each other; every filter subsumes itself. A filter whose first level is a wildcard never subsumes one whose first level is a literal `$`-level, since leading wildcards do not match `$` topics (§4.7.2). |

## Mdns.kt { #mdns-kt }

A dependency-free multicast DNS and DNS-SD implementation, sized to advertise and find OSCQuery
services on the local network.

[`Mdns`](networking.md#mdns-kt-mdns) answers queries for the services an [`OscQueryServer`](networking.md#oscqueryserver-kt-oscqueryserver) registers and runs the one-shot
browse behind `Box.oscQueryDiscover`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/io/osc/query/Mdns.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/io/osc/query/Mdns/)

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">Mdns</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/io/osc/query/Mdns/#L36)

Just enough multicast DNS (RFC 6762) and DNS-SD (RFC 6763) to advertise and find OSCQuery services, with no dependency: a responder that answers PTR/SRV/TXT/A questions for the services registered with [`advertise`](networking.md#mdns-kt--mdns--advertise), and a one-shot [`browse`](networking.md#mdns-kt--mdns--browse).

## OscQueryBox.kt { #oscquerybox-kt }

The box-facing OSCQuery entry points: `Box.oscQuery` to publish parameters, `Box.oscQueryRemote`
and `Box.oscQueryDiscover` to reach other services, and `Box.oscQueryMirror` to show a remote's
namespace as Field controls.

[`OscQueryServices`](networking.md#oscquerybox-kt-oscqueryservices) keeps one server per HTTP port across box runs and brings callbacks onto the
main Runloop; [`BoxOscQuery`](networking.md#oscquerybox-kt-boxoscquery) is the per-box view that owns the parameters a box declares.

## OscQueryCodec.kt { #oscquerycodec-kt }

Encodes and decodes the OSC 1.0 messages that OSCQuery sends in WebSocket binary frames.

[`OscQueryCodec`](networking.md#oscquerycodec-kt-oscquerycodec) works on byte arrays with no socket, which is what the WebSocket side of
[`OscQueryServer`](networking.md#oscqueryserver-kt-oscqueryserver) and [`OscQueryRemote`](networking.md#oscqueryremote-kt-oscqueryremote) needs; UDP traffic goes through JavaOSC instead.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/io/osc/query/OscQueryCodec.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/io/osc/query/OscQueryCodec/)

### OscQueryCodec { #oscquerycodec-kt-oscquerycodec }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">OscQueryCodec</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/io/osc/query/OscQueryCodec/#L22)

The OSC 1.0 message encoding OSCQuery puts in WebSocket binary frames: an address, a type-tag string and big-endian arguments, each padded to four bytes. Handles `i f s d h T F N`, which is every type an OSCQuery parameter here can have; a bundle or an unknown tag decodes to `null`.

## OscQueryRemote.kt { #oscqueryremote-kt }

The client side of OSCQuery: [`OscQueryRemote`](networking.md#oscqueryremote-kt-oscqueryremote) reads another application's namespace over HTTP,
sets its parameters over OSC UDP, and follows changes over its WebSocket.

It talks to TouchDesigner, Max, Chataigne, VDMX or another Field, and finds them on the local
network with `OscQueryRemote.discover`. `OscQueryRoundTripTest` drives it against an
[`OscQueryServer`](networking.md#oscqueryserver-kt-oscqueryserver) in the same process.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/io/osc/query/OscQueryRemote.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/io/osc/query/OscQueryRemote/)

## OscQueryServer.kt { #oscqueryserver-kt }

The OSCQuery service Field publishes: a namespace of typed parameters served as JSON over HTTP,
set over OSC UDP, and pushed to WebSocket listeners.

[`OscQueryParam`](networking.md#oscqueryserver-kt-oscqueryparam) is one address with its type tags, value, range and set callbacks;
[`OscQueryServer`](networking.md#oscqueryserver-kt-oscqueryserver) holds the namespace and runs the HTTP/WebSocket and UDP sides. Box code usually
reaches it through `Box.oscQuery` in `OscQueryBox.kt` rather than constructing a server directly.

## Ltc.kt { #ltc-kt }

Linear timecode as audio: [`LtcEncoder`](networking.md#ltc-kt-ltcencoder) renders SMPTE LTC frames to samples, [`LtcDecoder`](networking.md#ltc-kt-ltcdecoder) reads
them back from a live or recorded signal, and [`TimecodeWav`](networking.md#ltc-kt-timecodewav) writes and reads the mono `.wav`
files LTC usually travels in.

[`LtcFrame`](networking.md#ltc-kt-ltcframe) is the 80-bit frame itself; [`LtcDecodedFrame`](networking.md#ltc-kt-ltcdecodedframe) is what the decoder reports for each
frame it finds. The decoder tolerates gain, DC offset, noise, speed changes and reverse play,
which `TimecodeTest` checks against encoder output.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/io/timecode/Ltc.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/io/timecode/Ltc/)

**Used in:** [SMPTE Timecode: LTC and MIDI Time Code](../smpte_timecode.md)

### LtcFrame { #ltc-kt-ltcframe }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">LtcFrame</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">timecode</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Timecode</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">userBits</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">colorFrame</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/io/timecode/Ltc/#L28)

One LTC (linear timecode) frame: the 80 bits SMPTE 12M records on an audio track once per video frame. Bits 0..63 carry the timecode in BCD interleaved with 32 user bits; bits 64..79 are the fixed sync word `0011 1111 1111 1101`, which tells a reader where a frame ends and which way the tape is moving.

### LtcEncoder { #ltc-kt-ltcencoder }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">LtcEncoder</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">rate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">TimecodeRate</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">sampleRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">48000</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">amplitude</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.5</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/io/timecode/Ltc/#L104)

Writes LTC as biphase-mark audio: the level flips at the start of every bit, and a 1 flips again half-way through. The output is a square wave between `-amplitude` and `+amplitude`; bit boundaries are placed on the nearest sample of the exact (fractional) position, so a long render does not drift even at 29.97.

## Mtc.kt { #mtc-kt }

MIDI Time Code for Field's MIDI ports: [`Mtc`](networking.md#mtc-kt-mtc) builds quarter-frame and full-frame messages and
parses full frames, and [`MtcDecoder`](networking.md#mtc-kt-mtcdecoder) reassembles incoming messages into [`Timecode`](networking.md#timecode-kt-timecode).

The extension functions [`sendMtcFullFrame`](networking.md#mtc-kt--sendmtcfullframe) and [`sendMtcQuarterFrames`](networking.md#mtc-kt--sendmtcquarterframes) send from a `MidiOutput`,
and [`mtcDecoder`](networking.md#mtc-kt--mtcdecoder) attaches a decoder to a `MidiInput`. To follow MTC as a smooth clock, use
`TimecodeClock.followMtc`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/io/timecode/Mtc.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/io/timecode/Mtc/)

**Used in:** [SMPTE Timecode: LTC and MIDI Time Code](../smpte_timecode.md)

### MtcDecoder { #mtc-kt-mtcdecoder }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">MtcDecoder</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/io/timecode/Mtc/#L70)

Reassembles MTC into timecode. Hand it every incoming MIDI message with [`accept`](networking.md#mtc-kt--mtcdecoder--accept) (or [`acceptBytes`](networking.md#mtc-kt--mtcdecoder--acceptbytes)); it ignores anything that is not MTC. [`current`](networking.md#mtc-kt--mtcdecoder--current) is the most recent time and [`onTimecode`](networking.md#mtc-kt--mtcdecoder--ontimecode) fires for every full frame and for every completed quarter-frame cycle (forward or backward).

## Timecode.kt { #timecode-kt }

The SMPTE timecode value types: [`TimecodeRate`](networking.md#timecode-kt-timecoderate) (24, 25, 29.97 drop-frame, 30) and [`Timecode`](networking.md#timecode-kt-timecode),
a frame count at a rate with HH:MM:SS:FF labelling, parsing and arithmetic.

The LTC, MTC and clock code in this package all exchange [`Timecode`](networking.md#timecode-kt-timecode) values.
